最近@boros_fi 又对套利工具进行了更新，想写一写关于使用boros做到年化20%+的中性套利。

跨所的中性资金费套利，主要是捕捉两个所之间同一标的的费率差距，用中性的敞口达到收租的目的。以前的问题主要集中在执行麻烦，需要管四条腿，监控各种数据，而boros一直在简化用户需要的操作。

现在在boros上基本可以直接看：

哪些市场有 spread，
仓位有没有完整对冲，
扣掉融资和费用后的实际年化，
对应的清算价格。

同时可以使用boros开源脚本多空开仓一步到位。

另外，分享一个最近看到的boros上的案例：

0.65M 实际投入资本，最终年化 21.8% APR。

具体的流程是：

先在 Boros 找同标的在不同交易所之间的费率差
当时最大的一组 ETH 
Hyperliquid ETH YU：7.57%
Gate ETH YU：4.63%

然后分四条腿执行，Boros 的开源工具搭配 CrossEx 可以把这套流程进一步自动化：

1. Boros Short $4.65M Hyperliquid ETH YU
锁定约 7.57% 的固定 Funding 收益，同时支 Hyperliquid 实际产生的浮动 Funding。
2. Hyperliquid Short ETH Perp 收取实际浮动 Funding，与 Boros Short YU 支付的浮动 Funding 对冲。
3. Boros Long $4.37M Gate ETH YU 锁定约 4.63% 的固定 Funding 成本，同时收取 Gate 实际产生的浮动 Funding。
4. Gate Long ETH Perp 支付实际浮动 Funding，Boros Long YU 收取的浮动 Funding对冲，同时和 Hyperliquid 的 ETH 空单一起对冲价格敞口。

这样 Hyperliquid 一侧最终锁定约 7.57% 的固定资金费收益，Gate 一侧锁定约 4.63% 的固定 Funding 成本，中间大约 2.94% 的资金费差被固定下来。对应的浮动资金费基本互相抵消，ETH 的方向风险也通过一多一空对冲掉。

之后再用同样的方法，在 Hyperliquid、Gate、Binance 之间继续寻找最大的资金费差，这个案例一共搭了 9 条腿。再配合 CrossEx 提高保证金效率和资金利用率，最终用约 65.8 万 U 的资本，建立了约 $13.7M 名义仓位，97% 对冲。年化资金费差收益约 $168K，扣除约 $25K 年化费用以后，最终净 APR 约 21.8%。

来欣赏一下老外00后 P小将是怎么规划第一份工资的：

计划每天买1枚SOL，连续两年。

据这位 Reddit 网友自己透露，他今年22岁，刚大学毕业，两周后开始第一份工作，年薪8.3万美元，外加10%奖金。

他暂时和父母一起住，日常支出只有电话费和车费。目前手里已经有452枚SOL，并且全部拿去质押。

其中150枚的平均成本约为74美元，另外约300枚来自早期交易Meme币赚到的利润。

有意思的是，他现在反过来劝别人别碰Meme币：“如果当初没开始交易，我手里的钱可能还会更多。”

拿到第一份工资后，他准备开始新的实验：每天买入并质押1枚SOL，坚持两年。

这甚至不算传统定投。传统定投通常固定投入100美元，他固定的是SOL数量。SOL价格越高，每天需要拿出的钱反而越多。

评论区有人按当前价格算了一笔账，每天1枚SOL，相当于每月投入约3200美元。以他预计每月约5000美元的税后收入计算，大半份工资都要进入SOL。

有人问他，已经重仓成这样，为什么还要继续买？

他的回答比较CX：“我相信SOL被严重低估了，至少还能涨3倍。”

他的目标是在24岁时持有1000枚SOL。如果SOL涨到300至400美元，他希望靠这笔钱获得随时旅行和换一种生活方式的自由。

现在00后P小将都这么勇吗？开局自带400 SOL，还要赚的更多。

不过，帖子评论区更有意思，可以看到两代加密玩家的碰面。

有人经历过SOL从290美元跌回50美元，最惨时浮亏66%；还有人曾把一半仓位压在LUNA上，又买过跌去95%的AI币。他们劝这个年轻人至少留点现金。

另一边的回复就简单得多：“五年后你会赚疯。”

在上一代人讨论分散配置、熊市回撤和黑天鹅时，新一代年轻人觉得自己还有时间，还有工资，应该搏一把。

没有人永远年轻，但永远有年轻人。

text:
Verifiable and private AI @near_ai provides not just privacy for people and businesses but also a safety tool.

Every interaction hashed and signed with attestation of exactly prompt and code/model run creating a provenance log useful for monitoring and forensics.

No more agents rewriting their own logs, not knowing which exact model or quantization was used post factum, routers switching things mid stream, and many other vectors. 

Out of process inspection (like Jev classifier model) can scan attested logs for any suspicious behavior: not just model behavior but also policy violation or security incidents.

text:
I just read what Zuck wrote about Muse connectors.

A few things I think this means:

1. We’re witnessing the agentification of consumer apps. 

2.  Zuck believes Muse reaching 100M+ users feels entirely possible. 

3. Whoever you connect to becomes your new landlord, so pick carefully.

4. Connectors become the new app listings (valuable real estate).

5. Being early could be as valuable as being early to the App Store in 2009.

6. Meta sees what people want, which providers convert, and what users will pay. That gives it the power to rank connectors, charge for distribution, and launch competing services.

7. The opportunity map includes agent native APIs, connector agencies, SEO for agents, identity and reliability infrastructure, and vertical connector marketplaces.

8. We’re moving from humans choosing apps to agents choosing businesses.

9. Every business will need an agent strategy, just like every business needed a mobile strategy.

10. Kinda crazy to say but a 3 person API company could reach 10M+ users through one great connector.

11. Connectors could create an entirely new second-order economy. The biggest opportunity may be helping businesses distribute, price, and optimize their services for agents.

12. Your API becomes more important than your app. Weird to think about but true.

13. Zuck wants Muse to own the moment between wanting something and getting it. He is coming for the app economy. Will he win? Right now it's Instinct vs Muse vs Grokbot. TBD.

text:
Here we go again! The WSJ is working on a story blaming Coinbase and me personally for the CLARITY Act not passing.

The Journal has repeatedly been hostile to CLARITY in its reporting, regurgitating bank lobby talking points, while I’ve spent years pushing for crypto legislation, but that’s not stopping them from trying to reverse the blame.

The boring TLDR: in January I opposed a draft of the bill going into a committee vote, because it needed a lot of work on DeFi, tokenization, CFTC authority, and stablecoin rewards. At the time, the bill had major issues that would have harmed crypto. Support was fractured, and it wasn’t passable. We worked with a number of parties who improved the bill and made it passable. All four of the items I called out were fixed in the draft that then went through the committee about four months later. I'm proud to have done it, and would do it again, because it helped create a better bill. One step of many along the way.

The final draft of CLARITY that went to the Senate was great, and I strongly supported it. I'll continue showing up for our customers and pushing for clear rules that treat crypto fairly, even if those who feel threatened by crypto try to plant false stories. It's a shame that the WSJ takes direction from bank lobbyists instead of reporting the truth, but luckily, people are smart enough to see through it these days, and it backfires on them every time.

SuperStables = Stripe/1inch for AI Agents

Let an agent discover any service it needs, figure out how to pay for it, route the payment, and complete the transaction autonomously.

➡️AI inference
➡️Compute
➡️Market data

➡️Financial services

The bigger vision

x402 / MPP / ACP

Different facilitators

Instead of an agent figuring all of that out itself:

Agent → SuperStables → Discover → Route → Pay → Receive Service

SuperStables is trying to become that abstraction layer.

Eventually the vision expands into treasury management, stablecoin yield, RWAs and tokenized equities as well.

author: jillgun
quoted_text:
There is hyperventilation about AI right now. Some say the worry is overblown and others are convinced we’re doomed.

Regardless of the rhetoric, there won’t be any slowing down. The monetary, political and security game dynamics guarantee that. It’s a race to get there first and there is no stopping it. How we build safety, whether we regulate, and how we cooperate will be a dynamic, unpredictable process. I applaud all who are in the arena doing their best to exercise their best judgment. 

Humanity is going to do its thing and…wing it.

Where does that leave us?

So what do we mortals do? Where can we find stability of emotion and thought amidst the turbulence? 

I have a suggestion for you. 

Say yes. 
To the experience and not the outcome. 
Bask in the glory of this moment. 
We are headed for the singularity.
The apex experience of an intelligent race.

I had a trial run doing this a few months ago when I did the entheogen 5-MeO-DMT. It’s the most powerful psychedelic on earth. 

I live streamed it.

It was, without question, the most profound experience of my life. It rendered me dumbfounded and speechless. My consciousness settled onto a single concept: the insane, impossible-to-comprehend preciousness of our existence. 

To arrive at that understanding, I had to navigate a gauntlet that threatened my sanity. 

Seconds after the 5-MeO-DMT enters your body, you are transported into what feels like a different realm of existence. The molecule then poses a question to you: will you relinquish control or shall I crush you?

If you say no, you’re annihilated and become trapped in a hellscape that has no exit.  Primal panic overwhelms. 

If you say yes, you are allowed entrance to take one step deeper into this new realm. Then the 5-MeO-DMT asks you again, yes or no. 

Each time you say yes, it gets harder to bear the immensity of the terrain. You’re constantly teetering on losing your mind in an expanse that is exhilarating beyond description.

Your only job is to say yes.

Yes to… absolutely… everything. 
No hesitation. 
No conditionals. 
No stated preferences. 

Your essence must emanate acceptance of all things. 

If you make it through, you arrive at the peak experience of conscious existence. The crown jewel which has no peer.

This is where I think we are heading and what awaits us.

I think the coming years will feel like a 5-MeO-DMT experience for every single one of us.  We may feel the crushing weight of uncertainty, speed of change, lack of control, and perceived psychosis.

We will feel challenged in ways that we cannot currently imagine. We will feel primal panic and be uncertain if we can stop ourselves from psychological unraveling. 

The antidote isn’t more control or more knowing, it’s acceptance. 

This is not giving up or shying away from the fight. It’s calming the core and stabilizing your system to give you strength and stamina and avoid being taken over by the primal panic.

In previous times of my life, I would have caved to 5-MeO-DMT. I didn’t have the physical, emotional, spiritual and psychological wherewithal. 

I encourage you to start practicing now. Whether in meditation, breathwork or prayer, take on the most complex issues of your life and arrive at full acceptance. One small step at a time. 

Things do not need to resolve as you want, or expect. Your only job is to say yes more thoroughly than you’ve ever said yes before.

We talk a lot about the technology, about what AI can do and what we think it will be able to do. What we don’t talk about much is the spiritual strength we will each need to navigate this transition. 

We will need each other more than ever before, and we will need to summon a capacity that currently feels foreign to us.

What lies on the other side? No one knows.

This may be the first singularity event in the universe.

在动辄上万亿美金估值和技术霸权的商业竞争里，让OpenAI或Anthropic单方面放慢脚步做安全合规，无异于拱手把市场和领先地位送给对手，这造成了典型的「囚徒困境」局面！

今天马斯克提出的「交叉红队测试框架」，是一个很好的解决当下AI安全问题的有效方案。相当于引入竞争性的第三方监督机制，打破了过去实验室“自发监管、自我审计”的自律方案！

text:
Crypto story you can use to impress a girl:

The story of a 50,676 $BTC Silk Road theft, a 9-year escape, and one ridiculous mistake that got him busted

Back in 2012, James “Jimmy” Zhong found a bug in Silk Road’s withdrawal system

And the exploit was almost stupidly simple

In one example, Zhong deposited 500 $BTC, then triggered five 500 $BTC withdrawals within the same second. Silk Road processed all five before updating his balance, leaving him with a 2,000 $BTC profit from that one move

He repeated this through multiple accounts and more than 140 rapid transactions until he had taken around 50,000 $BTC

$BTC was around $12 at the time, so the whole stash was worth roughly $600K

Zhong later claimed that he told Silk Road founder Ross Ulbricht, aka Dread Pirate Roberts, about the bug and was allowed to keep the coins

Then he basically disappeared with the money

He barely touched most of the stash through multiple bull markets. When Bitcoin Cash forked in 2017, his 50K $BTC also gave him roughly 50K bitcoin-cash:native, which he later converted into another ~3,500 $BTC

The funny part is how he eventually got exposed

In 2019, someone broke into his house and stole around 150 $BTC

So the guy who stole Bitcoin from Silk Road... called the police because someone stole Bitcoin from him

That report later became useful to investigators

Then Zhong made another small mistake: some Silk Road-linked $BTC eventually touched a KYC exchange account tied to his identity. Blockchain tracing, exchange records and the local police investigation helped connect everything back to him

In November 2021, authorities raided his home

They recovered around 50,676 $BTC worth roughly $3.36B at the time, plus cash, physical Bitcoins and other assets

Some of the private keys were hidden in a floor safe. Another wallet was stored on a small computer hidden inside a popcorn tin in his bathroom closet

Almost 9 years of hiding 50K+ $BTC ended with blockchain tracing, a KYC trail and a popcorn tin

Zhong later pleaded guilty to wire fraud and was sentenced to just 1 year and 1 day in prison, but lost all the $BTC

Moral of the story:

If you hold crypto, don't call 911

text:
Jev的产品和宣发都很顶尖，从冷启动、创作者模版、相关群体的有机互动，都值得学习下，整个故事还要从创始人包装说起。

一个1500粉的号，两年没发声，9月15日一句 “After co-inventing ChatGPT” 把stealth产品、新模型类别、DCVC领投的4000万融资一次性打出去，主帖收获两千万+浏览。创始人履历确实很硬，InstructGPT核心作者，但是确实话术也做了包装，RLHF不是他一个人发明的，与此同时，ChatGPT也没有所谓的发明人。

1/ 宣发并非自然爆发，而是高投入冷启动

https://t.co/JT8BDPWJQD 接了内容策略、发布包和当天seeding。创始人号从约1500涨到9万+，官号从200到6万+。宣发预算打满后，在发布后第一小时就铺天盖地把工程师和founder们时间线填满了Jev内容。

冷启动种子是买的，但后面几千万浏览是算法主动承接。一场大约十万美元级别的发布战役，撬出平均launch二十多倍的曝光，ROI可以说非常好了。

2/ 创作者侧的模版化生产

用心留意的朋友，应该会观察到Jev相关内容反复出现同一套结构：先一句“LLM写字 / Jev做决定”，再塞工单路由、风控、agent选工具，最后一段屏幕录像。Mario、Doom、Browser Use找航班，全是同一套演示语法。

还有一句比RLCD好传播一百倍的产品句：输出token定价为零。创作者不需要理解训练方法，复述“$0.042/M输入、输出免费、70–500ms”就够了。

模版的作用是让技术观众在不同账号上反复撞见同一个可理解的差异。看起来像有机讨论，但底层是可复制、低成本的叙事零件。

3/ 第一批技术群体跟上，铺量后飞轮效应出现

英文圈先行发动，Vercel高管公开测分类任务，有人开源约束解码复刻，有人把Jev接进browser agent。三天内社区冒出LiteLLM透传、Instructor预设、Pi路由插件、jev-browser、两个MCP server，中文圈接着快速承接。

而真实用户，吐槽也不少，比如有人拿到key之后发现打游戏泛化不如Astra，强项是快和便宜，这种帖比重复200x口号更真实可信。

4/ 渠道接棒，平台开始借它给自己引流

9/16 Vercel AI Gateway上架，官方称付费团队24小时渗透约13%，历史最快，随即把Jev免到9月25日

9/18 OpenRouter上架 typesafe/jev-1.13，只走Decisions端点，chat/completions直接拒绝

这些平台在用当下最快冷启动的模型给自己的Gateway获客，飞轮效应进一步加速。

5/ 链路复盘

创始人给一句可核验的身份，适当包装
产品差异压成对比句和一个反常识定价，让创作者能直接套模版
发布当天只服务第一小时，剩下交给算法
发动顶级平台一起 co-PR，启动互利飞轮

when i first joined amber's vc team, i used to overly care about the "tech". i would get so involved in it, akin to someone caring about rare traits on a nft or something. i think any other vc analyst would agree if they ever bull posted the "modular chain thesis".

i had the opportunity to watch a lot of projects launch. their pre-tge plans, and how it played out post-tge. most project's token performance did not live up to expectations. its not that the tech was bad, it was that the token was set up to fail due to predatory token allocations. however if you purely optimized for the tech and not the token dynamics, you lost!

right now to me, only 2 things matter. proof of work coins and memecoins. both can truly be fair, with no predatory supply overhang. however, both can also be unfair. trenchers know this when a coin is bundled. i think the same is true for proof of work, you always need to ask yourself is this game im playing fair?

when i see a project that does it "right", or atleast, what i would do myself if i launched a coin, i get interested.

A few days ago, a friend told me to take a look at $SCHIFFY, but I was too busy and forgot about it. Now the token’s market cap has already reached $7.3M. Honestly, I regret missing it, but let’s still take a closer look at what this token is about.

0x42afa2124ca5a2b83898e46b2da9a190995b1e18 

SCHIFFY is not simply a Gold Meme. Its deeper narrative is Moku gaming IP + Robinhood Chain + Tokenized Gold + Holder Rewards + Buyback/Burn.

SCHIFFY currently uses Tokenized GLD as its trading pair. Of the fees generated from trading, the SCHIFFY side is used for 100% Burn, while around 90% of the GLD side is distributed to SCHIFFY holders and 10% goes to the Treasury. So it has both holder yield + deflationary mechanisms. The higher the trading volume, the more GLD holders receive, and the more SCHIFFY gets burned.

But I think what really gives it a higher valuation is not the Gold Meme itself, but the Moku behind it.

Moku is a Web3 gaming team that has been operating for years. It has participated in ecosystems such as Axie Infinity, Pixels, and Grand Arena, and has its own gaming products and user base.

Moku is now integrating SCHIFFY into its gaming ecosystem, including Nomgar, Grand Arena S2, Super Battle Moki, Break, and a game of its own for SCHIFFY. One of the more important designs is that part of the future revenue generated by these games will be used to buy SCHIFFY and deposit it into the Vault.

So there are actually two flywheels here:

First layer:SCHIFFY Trading Volume ↑ → GLD Fees ↑ → Holder Rewards ↑ → More Holding/Attention ↑ → SCHIFFY Trading Volume ↑

At the same time:SCHIFFY Trading → Fees → Buyback/Burn → Supply ↓

Second layer:Moku Games → Game Revenue ↑ → Buy SCHIFFY → SCHIFFY Demand ↑ → Moku Ecosystem Attention ↑ → More Players/Revenue

This is also the biggest difference between SCHIFFY and a typical Meme: it is trying to evolve from a “Gold Meme” into a “Moku Gaming Ecosystem Token.”

The market is currently trading a combination of several narratives:Meme IP → Gold → Tokenized Gold → Robinhood Chain → Holder Rewards → Burn → Moku Gaming → Game Revenue → SCHIFFY Buyback

What really needs to be validated next is not simply the market cap, but several key metrics:

- SCHIFFY/GLD trading volume — determines whether the Fee Economy can sustain itself.

- Actual GLD distributed to holders — shows whether the yield mechanism is actually generating value.

- Actual SCHIFFY burned — confirms whether trading volume is translating into supply reduction.

- Moku game revenue — especially Nomgar and Grand Arena S2.

- Moku → SCHIFFY Buyback — this is the key to whether the second flywheel can actually work.

- Actual SCHIFFY usage within the games — if players start using SCHIFFY in practice, that is when it truly moves from a Meme into the Moku ecosystem.

So I would currently describe SCHIFFY as:A Robinhood Chain Meme that is trying to connect Moku’s gaming IP, Tokenized Gold, holder yield, and game-revenue buybacks.

The premium the market is giving it right now is essentially pricing in the future value capture SCHIFFY could receive from the Moku gaming ecosystem.

The real catalyst is not another KOL. It is whether this chain can actually work:Moku Games Launch → Generate Real Revenue → Revenue Buys SCHIFFY → SCHIFFY Becomes More Integrated Into the Gaming Ecosystem.

text:
这周美联储加息了，科技股反而涨了两天，利率和股价到底什么关系

周三美联储把联邦基金利率抬了25个基点，目标区间到3.75%到4%，这是2023年以来第一次加息，12票全票通过

加息当天市场几乎没动，接下来两天，纳斯达克从25978点涨到26522点，涨了2.1%

按教科书的说法，利率涨，股票该跌。结果反着来

先给一个短答案。利率管的是估值的地心引力，时间越长越管用，时间越短越不管用

拆开说。一家公司值多少钱，等于它未来能赚到的现金流，除以一个折现率。利率上去，折现率上去，分母变大，同样一笔现金流算出来的合理价就低。这条线拉长到十年二十年，谁也别想躲

但市场交易的是预期差。加息25个基点这种事，一个月前就被交易掉了。真到宣布那天，悬着的事落地，反而成了利空出尽。所以短期股价和利率经常反着走，一点都不稀奇

想明白这条慢变量，就得看2022年12月那篇《Sea Change》。它讲的正好是利率的长期方向怎么决定一代人的赚钱方式

它的骨架是这样。干投资53年，周期、狂热、恐慌、泡沫、崩盘都见过，真正算得上时代转向的只有两次，第三次正在进行

第一次转向在70年代。立法让高收益债对普通投资人敞开了门，买垃圾债从不体面变成正经生意。跟着变的是脑子，风险从必须躲开的东西，变成可以定价、可以买卖、可以承担的东西

这中间夹着一场硬仗。73到74年石油禁运点着了通胀，油价一年里从24美元跳到64美元一桶，CPI从72年的3.2%涨到74年的11%，到1980年还有13.5%。沃尔克1980年把联邦基金利率提到20%，到83年才把通胀按到3.2%

第二次转向安静得多。联邦基金利率在80年代末降到个位数高位，90年代落到个位数中段，四十年利率一路下行的环境从这儿开始

这段行情有多肥，标普500从1982年8月的102点涨到2022年初的4796点，年化回报10.3%。做投资这辈子最大的运气，就是赶上这四十年

道理不复杂。低利率是一颗便宜药，消费者借钱消费便宜，公司借钱扩张便宜，资产的估值跟着水涨船高。2009年到2020年初这颗药一直开着，疫情把经济按停之后，美联储几周之内就把当年救危机的方案加大量级又放了一遍，上一次用了几个月

药不可能一直便宜。利率抬上去，大家要求的回报就高，股票的合理价值就往下走。这是算术

那份判断给出来的未来是这几条

未来12到18个月会来一次衰退

企业盈利和投资人情绪一起变差

违约率会抬起来

利率不会从当时的位置往下走2000个基点

还有一句最要命的，过去13年、过去40年管用的那套打法，未来几年很可能不再是跑赢的那一套

三年过去，账是这么结的

利率这条方向说对了，幅度差得远。联邦基金利率2023年8月见顶5.33%，一路降到今年8月的3.63%，一共170个基点，和2000个基点差了一个数量级。这周加回25个基点，现在在4%附近，还是比2023年的峰值低一百多个基点

衰退没来。全国经济研究所的衰退指标到现在还是0

股市最不客气。标普500从2022年12月19日的3817点涨到本周的7637点，三年翻了一倍

三条里准了一条，错了一条，被打脸一条

那这篇东西还剩什么用。剩下的是那条慢变量。利率决定估值，价格决定命运，环境变了打法就得换。这三句话不看年份

回到开头那个问题。加息这天科技股为什么能涨，因为它交易的是预期差和情绪。而未来十年股票值多少钱，由利率的长期方向定

这两件事同时成立，不矛盾。只有把时间尺度看错的人，才会觉得矛盾

唯一不变的就是变化，环境换了，策略也要改

With Stock Tokens TVL reaching over $170M and nearly $50B in DEX volume on the Robinhood Chain, we are getting more questions about what they are and how they work.

All Robinhood Stock Tokens are backed 1:1 with real shares in secure custody. And Stock Tokens receive the economic equivalent of dividends and corporate actions returns reinvested into their holdings.

In other words, when a new Stock Token is minted, we buy a real share of the company at the same time.

What about in-kind redemption and voting rights? Not yet, but they’re coming. Step one is to scale adoption of Stock Tokens. We’re actively working on redemptions for shares 1:1 with voting for eligible Stock Token holders on the roadmap. We know how to do this well: we run a shareholder engagement platform, Say by Robinhood, which allows shareholders to participate in actions like voting.

What about the technology? We built Stock Tokens to be composable, which allows developers to build new innovative offerings like we have seen the past few weeks, with many that we have yet to discover.

What am I the most excited about? Billions of people in the world don't have access to U.S. investment assets. With Stock Tokens, that era is ending. Any eligible customer with a phone and an internet connection can now get exposure to the most exciting market in the world.

text:
Here we go again! The WSJ is working on a story blaming Coinbase and me personally for the CLARITY Act not passing.

The Journal has repeatedly been hostile to CLARITY in its reporting, regurgitating bank lobby talking points, while I’ve spent years pushing for crypto legislation, but that’s not stopping them from trying to reverse the blame.

The boring TLDR: in January I opposed a draft of the bill going into a committee vote, because it needed a lot of work on DeFi, tokenization, CFTC authority, and stablecoin rewards. At the time, the bill had major issues that would have harmed crypto. Support was fractured, and it wasn’t passable. We worked with a number of parties who improved the bill and made it passable. All four of the items I called out were fixed in the draft that then went through the committee about four months later. I'm proud to have done it, and would do it again, because it helped create a better bill. One step of many along the way.

The final draft of CLARITY that went to the Senate was great, and I strongly supported it. I'll continue showing up for our customers and pushing for clear rules that treat crypto fairly, even if those who feel threatened by crypto try to plant false stories. It's a shame that the WSJ takes direction from bank lobbyists instead of reporting the truth, but luckily, people are smart enough to see through it these days, and it backfires on them every time.

If OpenAI did not exist, what leverage would users actually have?

Anthropic should publish a clear explanation of how this happened.

text:
jev才发布几天，开源模型就复刻出来了！

可以看看 Mapika 开源的 decider-2b：一个完全不生成文本的语言模型。

它的核心思路是实现“系统一（快思考）”：输入上下文和带有选项的问题，模型会在一次前向传播（Single Forward Pass）中，直接返回各个选项的概率分布。

没有 Decoding 过程，不需要解析 JSON，也绝对不会出现 Schema 格式违规。它完全是为工程代码调用而设计的，而不是用来聊天。

核心数据与特性：
• 极致延迟：单次请求延迟仅 4.0 ms（开启 CUDA Graphs），批处理吞吐量高达 1670 次决策/秒（FP8）。
• 轻量底座：基于 1.9B 参数的 Qwen3.5-2B-Base 微调，支持最高 32k 上下文。
• 结构化输出：支持多选（最高 255 个选项）、布尔值和评分量表，且输出带有经过校准的置信度分数。

主要局限性：
目前仅支持英文，且该模型没有逻辑推理（Reasoning）能力。它本质上是一个超快、格式 100% 安全的模式匹配分类器。

非常适合用于客服工单路由、意图识别、内容风控等需要大规模、低延迟决策的业务场景。

https://t.co/BG8wdcwZjZ

1/ 最早接触 Bitcoin 是 2011 年看美剧《傲骨贤妻》，通过 Google 搜索了解后注册 Mt.Gox，第一次买时价格约 10 美元。不过这一集实际上是 2012 年 1 月才上的，不是 2011 年。

2/ 2012-2013 年写了一个做市商算法，参与 Just a Dice 的链上游戏，赚了 1 万个比特币

3/ OKX 是全球第一家上线莱特币 Litecoin 的平台，这为平台带来了海量流量。「一个品类资产成就一个交易平台」的典范 https://t.co/NB6Y4yDvSH

4/ 2017 年时过于保守，错过了投资以太坊的机会。其实 CZ 也很早认识 Vitalik，同样错过了投资以太坊的机会。

5/ 认识很多管几亿美元基金的朋友，结论是：没有任何基金能（长期）跑赢比特币。

6/ 「如果你连 10 个比特币都没有，就别来参加我们的行业大会，你算什么加密从业者」？之前在 OKX 大会上就说过了 https://t.co/J4XaC7eY4M

7/ 交易是一项严肃的工作。核心是严苛风控 + 强大的自控力，最重要的原则是「确保你始终留在牌桌上」。

8/ 创业成功最重要的三要素：运气 + 韧性 + 认知
author: minglaugodel
quoted_text:
在 #OKX年夜饭 上，@star_okx 还说了一个金句，后来被传播很广，我速记的时候漏掉了：作为行业的 KOL 要能长期吃到行业红利，一定要持有 $BTC. 如果一个 KOL 不持有 10 枚 (还有个说法是 5-10 枚) BTC，那就不是一个合格的 KOL。

在一个有近百名 KOL 的会上这样说，Star 很直率很赞 👍 今天看到 OKX 新一期 Jumpstart 支持 BTC 挖新币，也很拉好感。

无独有偶，@OneKeyHQ 创始人 @ohyishi 在  2023 年 11 月写了一篇文章《十币称侯》传播甚广，10 个 BTC 成为了一个重要的分水岭和心理锚点。

从 2017 年的千币侯，到 2021 年的百币侯，现在的十币称侯。核心资产的稀缺性更强了。

对于个人来说，追求链上的百倍币财富密码，和坚定持有比特币，两者之间并不矛盾。如何平衡好就考验个人能力了。

我也一直觉得，作为一个 KOL 是有「责任和义务」给更多新人推广、普及比特币相关知识的，不能只推广山寨币。君子爱财，取之有道。

text:
上个周期被大家冠以“天王级”的项目，如果还没发币，这个周期大概发不出来币了。

Linera 就是最新的样本。

之前由 a16z 等机构累计投资约 1200 万美元，创始人来自 Meta、参与过 Libra 稳定币项目，并试图用微链做出更低延迟、更接近 Web2 实时体验的 L1。

就是这样的 Linera，昨天宣布立即停运，因为计划代币$LNRA 社区轮公售 150 万美元，但实际只凑到不到 90 万，选择全额退款，后续紧急融资也失败。

这个资源和背景放在上个周期，那妥妥是大家预期无限拔高，交互内卷的项目。

但现在，一级市场和社区公售都更挑剔，大家更愿意给已经有真实使用和收入的项目付钱，而不是选择再给一条“还在路上”的 L1 付钱。

另一面是，老登公链已经被去魅。

链不再稀缺，TPS、最终性、新架构都讲过了，市场并不需要再多一条“技术更好”的新链。

但有意思的是，最近一些上个版本老登币还在涨。
留下来还有壳子的，代币或许会有炒作；没有代币、还没上主网的，真的连这个期权都没有了。

这轮周期很明显，技术已经不够被单独定价了。市场可以炒一个十年前的隐私币，也可以给已经有手续费的应用代币溢价，但大概率不会再给一条还没证明过非用它不可的新链预付未来。

大人，时代变了。

quoted_text:
作为一个过来人，我说一下终止全平 close position on stop 这个设计吧。。 

一般来说，这个设置就是在触发risk control （bot risk ratio < 1）和insufficient margin（保证金不足) 会把仓位全部平仓掉

这里的保证金又可以区分为：维持保证金，开仓保证金，单占用保证金，网格策略运行所需保证金等等等

大家可以看到这个设计的初衷就是为了“”控制风险“，相当于是一个止损点

为什么会有这个设计：是因为网格的计算比一般的合约还难（是一层层累加的），很多人是算不过来的（算得过来也不用这个了🤣） 

举个例子啊：按照你设计的网格，122后，将会累积到约5,250+个soxl （差不多是643k）按照20x的要求保证金需要33k左右，要是到118的话，保证金达到了40k左右

这里需要说的是：这个终止全平的设计是一个通用的设计，就我知道 @okx @Bybit_Official 都有类似的设计/选项供君选择 

看你说的情况应该是属于后者：开仓保证金不足，没办法开仓，系统判断为：终止，所以触发“终止全平”，所以系统帮你平仓

为什么开仓保证金不足也被系统认为应该“终止”，这个就涉及到网格策略的核心：连续性 ，网格是吃spread价差的，假设不能连续铺单子（出range）：原本自动循环的策略，开始出现缺单，实际交易行为偏离用户设置，就应该止损/不动

当然出现这种情况并不是一定平仓出局，你可以暂停/等，但是如果你选择了“终止平仓”，那系统就会按照你的设置来

你觉得因为是在上升趋势（从118-122），而系统提前帮你平仓所以你觉得亏了，最终损失1.4w+ ，而且随后价格122-128，你少了更多的预期收益

但你有没有想过，假设价格的路径是118 - 122 -110呢？ 这样看的话，你还能省一点

这个就是网格策略这个【终止全平】机制设置的意义 

而且grid合约的高杠杆网格策略天生就不适合大波动（即使是方向对的）。。。

quoted_text:
There are two ways AI progress could go very badly and that we must avoid.

First, we could lose control of the future to AI. This is unacceptable; we are unapologetically on Team Humanity, and AI must always serve people. To ensure that, we need ways to ensure that alignment and safety techniques stay ahead of progress in model capabilities.

Second, we could end up in a world with too much concentration of power. If an extraordinarily powerful AI is used by one person or company to impress their worldview onto everyone else, the results could be extremely dystopian.

Avoiding these two threats requires walking a narrow middle path; for example, one country could gain too much power. Another example is one lab ending up with too much power.

看你说的情况应该是属于后者：开仓保证金不足，没办法开仓，系统判断为：终止，所以触发“终止全平”，所以系统帮你平仓

为什么开仓保证金不足也被系统认为应该“终止”，这个就涉及到网格策略的核心：连续性 ，网格是吃spread价差的，假设不能连续铺单子（出range）：原本自动循环的策略，开始出现缺单，实际交易行为偏离用户设置，就应该止损/不动

当然出现这种情况并不是一定平仓出局，你可以暂停/等，但是如果你选择了“终止平仓”，那系统就会按照你的设置来

你觉得因为是在上升趋势（从118-122），而系统提前帮你平仓所以你觉得亏了，最终损失1.4w+ ，而且随后价格122-128，你少了更多的预期收益

但你有没有想过，假设价格的路径是118 - 122 -110呢？ 这样看的话，你还能省一点

这个就是网格策略这个【终止全平】机制设置的意义 

而且grid合约的高杠杆网格策略天生就不适合大波动（即使是方向对的）。。。

我在125的时候开仓了SOXL网格机器人
投入保证金大约45000u
设置的交易区间为122至127
我在125开仓完成后
价格很快下跌到122区间下限
机器人随即暂停交易
这个时候我查看了账户安全
显示机器人余额3万u左右

我预设的止损价格为118
价格跌破122后继续向下回落
全程没有跌破118止损价位
账户没有触发止损 没有策略终止 也没有爆仓
最低118附近时候
我查看了账户大约剩余1万多u

后续行情从低位118附近开始反弹
重新回升至122区间位置
按照机器人正常逻辑
此时应该重新启动正常交易
直到触发127止盈终止

这一轮反弹行情很好
最终价格突破128
也成功触及我设置的127止盈点位
我手动测算本次行情本该盈利12500U左右
账户应该有差不多6万u了

但我随后打开账户实际账户结果
机器人在122时候被强平
币安产品给的理由是
我设置了终止全平
我账户余额只有大约3万u

保证金不足终止交易强平可以理解
但机器人第一次下跌到122时没有终止策略
从122下探至118保证金也足够没有爆仓
但从118反弹回升回到122的这一刻
直接被系统强制平仓终止策略
也就是我承担了亏损及爆仓的全部风险
终于在要盈利的时候账户被强平了

币安的产品
混淆了维持保证金和机器人开仓保证金的区别
我问他们如果不是机器人账户
我用10x杠杠开合约
下跌时候不是维持保证金不足
而是新开仓保证金不足
币安有没有权利强平我的仓位？
币安的客服和pt团队还是尽心尽力的
一直在帮我沟通
但是这么明显的产品设计缺陷
为何一年多了还不改
是产品自己不用网格机器人
还是真不懂强平规则

我认为币安网格机器人存在产品设计缺陷
行情未触碰止损规则
却在反弹回归区间时非正常强平
导致本该到手的盈利变成亏损
用户在币安开机器人一旦触及区间下限
就变成了非对称风险
下跌你可能继续亏甚至爆仓
但上涨立即帮你强平
这样一个大所
产品是如何设计这样的产品锁定用户亏损的？
这是币安本意还是产品设计理念存在问题

类似的情况其实一年多前就有人反馈
但币安产品坚称这个方案没有问题

我给出的建议是
在反弹回122的时候
可以先处理平仓委托
暂不执行开仓委托
直到机器人足够保证金开仓委托

客户开仓机器人是为了来赚钱的
不是为了来锁定亏损的
我开过很多币安机器人
只有这个我留意了下是这样被强平的
你也可以留意下你回去的仓位
这不是bug是币安的产品设计理念
我肯定不是唯一受害者

text:
In the last crypto cycle, people were bearish on options vs. perps because perps are “easier to understand than options and we need to onboard the masses.”

That was such a bad take because:
 
1. Massive amounts of retail traders learned options during the GME COVID era just fine.

2. Just because it’s “easy to understand” doesn’t mean it’s good for retail traders. Futures are easier to understand than options, yet I’d sooner recommend a friend a long call option than a futures contract because futures will wipe them out if they are wrong.

3. People in crypto like memecoins and the asymmetric upside they provide. Options (especially long calls) are the traditional market equivalent, not perps. 

4. Crypto is obsessed with composability, and options are the most composable financial product that enables you to express any opinion about the market. 

It’s great to see the leader in onchain options finally getting the attention they deserve: @DeriveXYZ

text:
可验证、且保护隐私的 AI @near_ai 提供的不只是面向个人和企业的隐私保护，更是一套安全工具。

每一次交互都会被哈希并签名，附带关于「究竟运行了哪段 prompt、哪份代码/模型」的远程证明（attestation），由此形成一条可用于监控与取证的溯源日志。

从此不再有：Agent 自己改写自己的日志、事后无从得知到底用的是哪个模型、哪种量化版本、路由器在请求中途偷偷换模型，以及其他种种攻击向量。

进程外的独立检查（比如 Jev 分类器模型）可以扫描这些带证明的日志，识别任何可疑行为——不只是模型行为异常，也包括策略违规和安全事件。
author: NEAR_China
quoted_text:
Verifiable and private AI @near_ai provides not just privacy for people and businesses but also a safety tool.

Every interaction hashed and signed with attestation of exactly prompt and code/model run creating a provenance log useful for monitoring and forensics.

No more agents rewriting their own logs, not knowing which exact model or quantization was used post factum, routers switching things mid stream, and many other vectors. 

Out of process inspection (like Jev classifier model) can scan attested logs for any suspicious behavior: not just model behavior but also policy violation or security incidents.

text:
是，石油和天然气现金流是它起家的根本。但它能做这么大，还靠“把钱留下来、分散投资、持有几十年”的制度。 至于选标的，它的方式更接近“广泛持有全球企业，再做适度调整”。

你可以从三个方面理解。

第一，本金是怎么来的？

挪威1969年发现北海大型油田，1971年开始生产；1990年立法成立石油基金，1996年才把第一笔钱转进去。它的目标很明确：把终有一天会挖完的地下资源，变成后代也能享有的金融资产。 基金官方历史⁠￼

国家主要通过三种方式获得油气收入：向油气企业收税、直接持有油气田取得净收益，以及持有 Equinor 股权获得分红。这些国家油气净现金流进入基金，再按财政安排向政府预算拨款。政府收入来源⁠￼

第二，它怎么总能买到好标的？

你看到它持有很多优秀公司，首先是因为它买得足够广：

* 战略基准是 70%股票、30%债券。
* 股票基准以全球股票指数为基础，主要按公司市值分配权重。
* 截至2026年中，它持有约 7,100家公司，全球很多成长起来的企业都会在它的覆盖范围里。投资基准⁠￼、持仓概况⁠￼

所以，看到它持有一个大牛股，不能直接推断它早就精准预判了这家公司。 广泛持有市场，本来就有机会分享赢家的上涨，同时也会持有表现不好的公司。

它确实有专业团队分析企业，决定相对指数多买还是少买。但有个很能说明问题的数据：1998年至2026年中，基金年化回报约6.86%，每年超过基准约0.24个百分点。 我的理解是，它成功的主要部分来自长期参与全球市场，主动管理在此基础上增加收益。官方收益数据⁠￼

第三，石油现金流究竟有多重要？

非常重要：它提供了大量可长期投资的本金。但后来，投资收益已经超过政府累计投入。

截至2026年中，基金约22.68万亿挪威克朗的规模，来源大致如下：

来源累计金额约占基金规模
政府净注入资金5.51万亿克朗24%
投资回报15.21万亿克朗67%
汇率变动1.97万亿克朗9%

汇率部分是折算成挪威克朗产生的价值变化，需要与投资收益分开看。官方规模拆解⁠￼

还有一个关键：政府给花钱设了约束。 财政规则要求，长期使用基金的钱与预期实际回报相匹配，目前按基金价值的约3%估算，并允许随经济周期调整。这让大部分资本能够继续留在市场里复利。挪威财政规则⁠￼

如果你关注的是“现金流好，是否更容易把投资做好”，我的判断是：好的现金流让你有条件长期持有；分散配置和支出纪律，决定你能否真正把这个条件用好。 挪威把这几件事持续做了几十年。

text:
One thing I've really enjoyed recently is getting to witness the evolution of a product from the outside while being closely involved with the team.

Watching @EthenaPay go from 2 months ago to now has been a really interesting learning experience. I've been giving the team feedback along the way, and you get to see how users actually behave, what they care about, which assumptions were wrong, what needs to be fixed, and how the team adapts along the way.

I think that's something I really missed over the last few years.

Most of my recent jobs have been at blockchain infrastructure companies, where the product is usually the chain itself. There's obviously a lot to learn there too, but the feedback loop feels very different when you're building infrastructure compared to a product that people are actually using every day.

Honestly, it's made me realize how much I enjoy this side of building.

I don't think I want to work at a chain again anytime soon.

Give me an actual product with real users, messy feedback, and a million things to improve.

The Journal has repeatedly been hostile to CLARITY in its reporting, regurgitating bank lobby talking points, while I’ve spent years pushing for crypto legislation, but that’s not stopping them from trying to reverse the blame.

The boring TLDR: in January I opposed a draft of the bill going into a committee vote, because it needed a lot of work on DeFi, tokenization, CFTC authority, and stablecoin rewards. At the time, the bill had major issues that would have harmed crypto. Support was fractured, and it wasn’t passable. We worked with a number of parties who improved the bill and made it passable. All four of the items I called out were fixed in the draft that then went through the committee about four months later. I'm proud to have done it, and would do it again, because it helped create a better bill. One step of many along the way.

The final draft of CLARITY that went to the Senate was great, and I strongly supported it. I'll continue showing up for our customers and pushing for clear rules that treat crypto fairly, even if those who feel threatened by crypto try to plant false stories. It's a shame that the WSJ takes direction from bank lobbyists instead of reporting the truth, but luckily, people are smart enough to see through it these days, and it backfires on them every time.

text:
油价之后，食品涨价可能继续冲击债市

联合国食品价格指数已经涨到 2022 年底以来的最高水平。摩根大通预计，2027 年上半年，全球食品价格的同比涨幅可能达到 5%，高于今年同期的 2.8%。也就是说，接下来大家可能还要为吃饭多花钱，即便油价有所回落，食品涨价也可能让通胀迟迟降不下来。

原因是农作物生产受到影响，化肥供应又比较紧张，种粮食的成本上去了，产量还可能受到影响。再加上霍尔木兹的封锁，导致了粮食和化肥运起来更贵，这些增加的费用最后可能体现在超市和餐桌上。

而且粮食从种下去到收获需要时间，供应出现问题以后，很难马上补回来，加息也无法让地里立刻多长出粮食。

这也是债券市场担心的地方。物价一直涨，债券支付的固定利息就越来越不经花，投资者会要求更高的收益才愿意买，现有债券的价格就可能继续下跌。同时，通胀降不下来，央行也更难放心降息，政府和企业借钱就得继续承担较高的利息。

因此食品价格如果继续上涨，高利率就可能维持更久，风险市场也会继续受到影响。

quoted_text:
伊朗对霍尔木兹的封锁影响的不仅仅是石油还有粮食

前面我写过，霍尔木兹封锁导致的在油价之外还有化肥和粮食。现在这个影响已经开始在农产品价格上出现了。

彭博现货农业指数本月上涨接近 13%，是过去很多年里非常少见的单月涨幅。主要的原因就是战争和恶劣天气共同推动，尤其是霍尔木兹的封闭带来的化肥、能源和运输成本上涨已经开始影响粮食的价格了。

不止是粮食，中东还占全球尿素出口的 42%，氨出口的 27%，而这些都是农业大量使用的氮肥原料。霍尔木兹通行受阻以后，不同地区的氮肥价格相比战争以前已经上涨了 25% 到 50%。

目前上游的农产品已经先涨了，后边才会轮到食品加工、运输、批发，最后传到消费者买到的食品价格。摩根大通此前预计，这轮化肥冲击可能把全球食品通胀暂时推到 4% 到 5%，比较明显的影响会集中在 2026 年后期到 2027 年。

油价和运输成本仍然偏高，化肥供应没有完全恢复，同时全球天气又开始出现更多问题。这些综合在一起导致的就不仅仅是油价上涨和食品上涨，而是全球的通胀上升，消费力下降，而其中最重要的就是霍尔木兹，伊朗封锁的霍尔木兹导致的。

说实话，我到现在仍然无法理解认为伊朗封锁霍尔木兹是正义的代表，即便伊朗是在对抗美国，但代价就是全世界，这种全面的通胀上涨即便是中国都难以避免。

中国成品油最近一次调价是在 8月28日24时，国家发改委把汽油最高零售价每吨上调 375 元、柴油上调 360 元。以北京为例，92 号汽油从 7.78 元/升涨到 8.09 元/升，一次上涨 0.31 元。95 号从 8.29 涨到 8.61 元，上涨 0.32 元。

而且 8月14日 中国刚刚降过一次油价，北京 92 号当时从 7.97 降到 7.78 元。结果两周以后直接涨到 8.09 元，已经把前面的降幅全部涨回去还多了一些。如果霍尔木兹继续被伊朗封锁，中国的油价也还会继续上涨，甚至是化肥和粮食的价格也跑不了。

quoted_text:
More people should know about the Interfold.

It's basically what I've been yelling at people to build with the MACI ideas ( https://t.co/mlDy84zXQo ) for almost a decade, and now it exists, in a generalized form.

The idea is: a privacy protocol optimized for things like voting (and other use cases eg. secret-ballot auctions). The mechanism generates a threshold encryption key, and people send in their votes onchain, using a ZKP to prove eligibility. An arbitrary computation on the votes gets run inside FHE, and then threshold-decrypted.

From what I can tell (the docs are good https://t.co/adzwK6ezMN ), it gets pretty optimal security guarantees:

* Voter anonymity can be made unconditional if eligibility is proven with ZK-SNARKs
* Censorship resistance is guaranteed by ethereum (votes can be posted directly onchain, and there's a proof that all posted votes are taking into account)
* The correctness of the outputted result can be ensured via ZK over FHE
* Liveness and coercion resistance depend on M-of-N honesty; unavoidable given present-day technology

The main limitation is that today "ZK over FHE" is only properly available for additive vote tallying, as it's too expensive for computations that involve multiplication or other more complicated manipulation at the moment. There's work in progress on slashing-based / optimistic computation for such situations.

(And of course ideally in the long term we'd figure out obfuscation so you can get rid of the M-of-N committees😃)

这个世界上努力的人很多，真正能拿到大结果的人永远只是少数，所以如果你到现在还没有赚到很多钱，也没有抓住所谓的人生大机会，真的不用气馁，更不需要焦虑，因为很多时候真正把人拖垮的，并不是暂时没有结果，而是在一个离金钱很近、所有人都在展示结果的环境里，不知不觉开始拿自己和别人比较，别人赚钱，你觉得自己落后，别人暴富，你觉得自己错过，最后每天接收了大量信息，却只留下了内耗。

越是在这种时候，越要安住其心，把注意力从别人身上收回来，从纷乱的信息里只提取真正对自己有用的东西，然后继续照顾好自己的身体、情绪、判断和节奏。

你要记得，这个世界本来就是你一个人的游戏，别人比你快一点、赚得多一点、暂时站得高一点，其实都和你没有那么大的关系，你真正要做的，只是把自己的这一局继续玩好。独善其身，是这个时代最被低估的能力，也是对抗长期内耗最有效的解药。

text:
🇨🇭Switzerland has adopted its new security strategy, and some of the contents are unprecedented. Perhaps this is another signal showing where we all are in current circumstances. I note down some interesting details.
The strategy describes a coming European “window of vulnerability” where Europe may still be building up its defence capabilities while being less able to rely fully on US support, as Russia continues to strengthen its war economy. In that period, Russia could intensify hybrid operations and potentially attack further European states.

1. The redefinition of Swiss “neutrality” is unprecedented. It is also unexpected. I will not use the cliché “this is not surprising”, because it kind of is! The broadened “armed attack” framing that takes cyber / hybrid activity seriously and as potential signals towards, or of, an armed attack is compatible with NATO thinking and perhaps motivated by it. The implied logic stands out. If a neighboring state is subject to an armed attack and Switzerland at the same time is a target/victim of hybrid attacks by the same aggressor, this must be taken into account when Switzerland assesses if it is itself under an armed attack. If it reaches that conclusion, Switzerland can respond within the armed conflict, becoming a party to it. Adding the “hybrid attack” ingredient can  be read as a modern way of identifying the threshold AND the context (the ultimate decision remains political, true). Still, it is a long road from the Paris Treaty of 1815.

2. The strategy’s signals about reliance on the United States are impossible to miss. The document  states quite openly that the United States no longer sees itself as the guarantor of the international order as we knew it or of European security, and that it considers the defence of Europe to be the responsibility of European states. These are issues concerning true control and reliability of hardware and software. The strategy explicitly treats dependencies on foreign suppliers, information systems, cloud infrastructure and AI as a security issue and calls for them to be reduced where possible. The nature of technology and geopolitical changes converge here.

3. The emphasis on the risks of disinformation and influence operations is very very strong, the strategy  allocates a lot of space to it. In Switzerland’s case this is naturally strategically coherent although I respectfully disagree that Switzerland faces significant risks of election interference (but it may: e.g. for referendums).

Considering the information space as a national security domain in the technical sense (rather than a media domain or a media sense) should be the way forward. I wonder though if the way the response to disinformation is distributed across Swiss institutions would be effective in practice. I doubt it. Interdepartmental teams are proper until they aren’t. I’d say today that they no longer are a good approach.

4. Major omission. The lack of explicit coverage of cognitive operations is an intriguing but evident weakness of the strategy.

这个世界上努力的人很多，真正能拿到大结果的人永远只是少数，所以如果你到现在还没有赚到很多钱，也没有抓住所谓的人生大机会，真的不用气馁，更不需要焦虑，因为很多时候真正把人拖垮的，并不是暂时没有结果，而是在一个离金钱很近、所有人都在展示结果的环境里，不知不觉开始拿自己和别人比较，别人赚钱，你觉得自己落后，别人暴富，你觉得自己错过，最后每天接收了大量信息，却只留下了内耗。

越是在这种时候，越要安住其心，把注意力从别人身上收回来，从纷乱的信息里只提取真正对自己有用的东西，然后继续照顾好自己的身体、情绪、判断和节奏。

你要记得，这个世界本来就是你一个人的游戏，别人比你快一点、赚得多一点、暂时站得高一点，其实都和你没有那么大的关系，你真正要做的，只是把自己的这一局继续玩好。独善其身，是这个时代最被低估的能力，也是对抗长期内耗最有效的解药。

祝你在这个牛市玩得愉快，也祝你赚到钱之后，心里依获得平静。Love & Peace From 小毛哥 ❤

text:
我应该算中文博主里少数聊 Hookr的人了。

庆幸的是， robinhood:0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c 从底部上来3x了，关键是这还是现阶段链上没啥行情的情况下，属于被链上大血洗错杀的币自我的“修复”行情，所以现在短时的价格表现也不能说明啥。

为什么涨？

说它是又一个“模块化”的Celestia $TIA ，会像上周期由模块化驱动的百链扩张一样，成为本周期Uniswap V4 Hooks组件扩张的关键组件；

说它会在链上对一键发币疲劳后，市场开始寻找业务逻辑复杂，有技术支撑的，正经Devs开发的有成长性的项目，它会成为沉淀和放大链上创新的必要基础设施；

说它和Uniswap Labs有着说不清道不明的暧昧关系，Uniswap能不能在众Launchpad大战背景下，持续稳坐流动性中枢的座椅，就需要Hooks能力的向外输出，而它作为Hooks的开放封装平台，打头阵；

Okay，说这些你如果还觉得“抽象”的话，说点你能听懂的！

最近SEC发布的重磅文件里，允许许可制AMM流动性池交易。有了一个许可，你会担忧和DeFi的无许可理念相悖，但Hooks作为一个外挂钩子，会成为大量老DeFi协议被纳入合规监管的必要组件，因为可以在beforeswap前加一切白名单，Allowlist，准入规则等等自定义规则都是Hookr的用武之地；

无论从牛市的技术创新PVE视角，还是从拥抱合规的TradFi和DeFi融合大叙事视角， @Hookrfun 所卡的生态位都很关键。

Note：最大的风险就是Hooks被卡死在若干限定的功能下，完全不需要大扩展，且Uniswap官方下场自己做Hooks广场，Hookr被沦为弃子。

但Uniswap能放弃和Pons争抢Launchpad，其实已经标明了态度，Hookr的机会和前景还很大。当前链上代币波动巨大，价值发现时间会很长，介意短期波动的勿喷，以上观点，仅供参考，DYOR!

我在上个牛市、上上个牛市的时候，从没有人跟我讲过这个道理，但我现在很想把这段话分享给新人们，算是肺腑之言了：

这个世界上努力的人很多，真正能拿到大结果的人永远只是少数，所以如果你到现在还没有赚到很多钱，也没有抓住所谓的人生大机会，真的不用气馁，更不需要焦虑，因为很多时候真正把人拖垮的，并不是暂时没有结果，而是在一个离金钱很近、所有人都在展示结果的环境里，不知不觉开始拿自己和别人比较，别人赚钱，你觉得自己落后，别人暴富，你觉得自己错过，最后每天接收了大量信息，却只留下了内耗。

越是在这种时候，越要安住其心，把注意力从别人身上收回来，从纷乱的信息里只提取真正对自己有用的东西，然后继续照顾好自己的身体、情绪、判断和节奏。

你要记得，这个世界本来就是你一个人的游戏，别人比你快一点、赚得多一点、暂时站得高一点，其实都和你没有那么大的关系，你真正要做的，只是把自己的这一局继续玩好。独善其身，是这个时代最被低估的能力，也是对抗长期内耗最有效的解药。

祝你在这个牛市玩得愉快，也祝你赚到钱之后，心里依获得平静。Love & Peace From 小毛哥 ❤

text:
Grok leads AA's streaming transcription benchmark, with 2.7% overall word error.

But I'd check the voice-agent results before choosing it for customer calls.

On AA-AgentTalk, final word error rates are:
- Muse Voice Transcribe: 2.7%
- ElevenLabs Scribe v2 Realtime: 2.8%
- Grok Voice Transcribe 2.0: 3.2%

Grok does better on parliamentary speeches and earnings calls, which helps its overall score. But those aren't the same as someone calling about a missing order.

AA-AgentTalk uses recordings designed around voice-agent interactions. It still isn't a live customer service test, but it changes what I'd shortlist.

Then there's timing.

Across the full benchmark, Grok's first post-speech transcript arrives after 490ms. Muse and ElevenLabs take about 130ms.

That's transcription after speech ends. It isn't the wait before a customer hears an answer.

I'd test STT, turn detection, LLM, TTS, and the phone connection together. Some stages overlap, so adding their advertised latencies won't tell us enough.

Saving time on transcription could let the LLM check something before answering. But answering early doesn't help if the customer hasn't finished talking. Neither does asking them to repeat an order number you misheard. I'd measure the wait until a useful spoken reply, alongside corrections and completed tasks.

If you're running phone agents, which change actually reduced repeats or interruptions?

CLARITY 法案推进受阻

美国参议院就 H.R. 3633《数字资产市场清晰法案》（CLARITY Act）进行程序性表决。从目前的现场报道看现在是 50-49 法案推进受阻。

这次最关键的门槛是 60 票。共和党有 53 席，即便全员支持，也需要至少 7 张民主党或独立议员的赞成票。如果有两三名共和党议员反对，需要争取的跨党支持就会上升到 9 至 10 票。

此前在参议院银行委员会阶段，支持推进法案的民主党议员只有 Gallego 和 Alsobrooks 两人。

从表决前的谈判看，主要分歧集中在三个方面。

第一，公职人员加密利益的限制，仍未谈拢。

民主党希望对总统等公职人员及相关家庭利益设置能够实际执行的约束。新版已经加入资产处置要求，并赋予州检察长部分伦理执法权，但民主党仍质疑这些条款能否直接约束总统，以及是否存在允许官员保留加密业务利益的例外。

第二，稳定币收益触及银行的存款利益。

社区银行等机构担心，稳定币的利息、收益和奖励会吸引存款流出，进而影响本地贷款能力。

新版提出在存款流失后采取限制措施，但银行业认为，等到大量存款已经流走再干预，保护力度仍然不够。这也让部分共和党议员的支持存在变数。

第三，开发者责任与执法权限，仍存在多方冲突。

DeFi 开发者应获得多大范围的保护、哪些平台需要承担监管责任，都是争议。与此同时，包括纽约州在内的 18 位州及哥伦比亚特区检察长联署反对现有文本，担心法案削弱他们依据现行法律打击加密诈骗的权力。

博彩组织则要求进一步限制预测市场提供体育赛事合约。不同组织希望修改的条款各不相同。

目前来看，2026年能实现 CLARITY 法案概率已经很低了。

text:
高净值以及小额投资者继续买入 Bitcoin

最近我一直说不清楚上涨的理由，有小伙伴给我留言说这就是牛市，牛市上涨没有理由，就像熊市下跌没有理由一样。对于这个回答我是能理解的，但现在是不是就是 bitcoin:native 的牛市我很难给出准确的判断。

但我确实愿意在 75,000 美元附近埋伏买入，而且从数据来看当美联储和日本都在加息的时候明显看到高净值投资者和小额投资者的链上地址都在增持 Bitcoin 。

高净值投资者就不说了，几乎是常年增持的典范，最近一年的数据中几乎都在增持，而小规模投资者则对价格更加敏感，最近也能看到在买入的趋势，所以虽然我对于“牛市”这个词还有些保守，但从 60,000 美元到现在投资者的买入情绪还是挺高的。

我比较担心的原因主要还是伊朗问题，如果油价还是保持在高位，对于美国经济的压力可能会继续上涨。

author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
美日加息并未因为 bitcoin:native 投资者恐慌抛售

美联储和日本加息的时候我都在关注 Bitcoin 的数据，尤其是会不会有恐慌抛售的数据出现，从目前来看即便是在会议的当天或者是准备加息的当周，又或者是提前一周两周都没有看到有大量 bitcoin:native 转移到交易所的数据。

这个数据蛮重要的，因为即便是到现在 DEX 已经很完善了，但如果现货抛售除了大型机构的 OTC 以外，更多的还是通过交易所执行的，所以转移到交易所的数据就能看出投资者，尤其是散户对于美联储和日本加息是不是出现担心的状态。

实际来看虽然本周二到周五转入量相比前两周稍微多了一点，但在一年的转移数据中仍然是处于较低的水平，这就说明虽然有部分的投资者会担心加息，但大多数的持仓者并没有过分担心，这也是 Bitcoin 价格较为稳定的原因之一。

text:
Jev might genuinely be an “Internet moment” for AI.

TypeSafe reports up to 193x faster and 444x cheaper performance in tests with Claude Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra.

@0xCodila just wrote a great 10-page article explaining what Jev is, how to use it, and where its 100x advantage comes from.

Here are the 10 steps:

1 → LLMs create. Agents act. Jev decides the next move.

2 → Turn agent forks into three primitives: Choice, Score and probability.

3 → Build with OpenAI, Anthropic or xAI first, then swap Jev in without rebuilding the graph.

4 → Start with shared state, parallel decisions, risk thresholds and an execution queue.

5 → Batch decisions instead of making them sequentially. In one test, 13 questions were 10x faster and 12.2x cheaper.

6 → Put Jev at bounded forks: agent, model, tool, browser action or human escalation.

7 → Benchmark the whole loop, not just individual model calls.

8 → Rank wide, read narrow: shortlist first, then spend compute on what matters.

9 → Reuse the same system: State → Questions → Action → Verify.

10 → Keep Jev out of math, writing and irreversible execution. Code computes, LLMs create, Jev decides.

The result:

A slow, expensive agent loop becomes a much faster decision system that can route, score and escalate in milliseconds.

text:
Encoder 的卷土重来

BERT 本来是一条极有潜力的路线：高效地把输入压成 representation。但它停留在了 task-specific 时代，每个任务都需要微调。

GPT 早期同样如此，后来却沿着 scaling、in-context learning 和 instruction tuning 走向了 泛化，把自然语言变成 universal task interface。分类、判断、推理、工具调用，统统变成 generation。

于是 decoder-only 赢下了整个 paradigm，encoder 也失去了继续探索 general classifier 和 general representation model 的历史机会。

但 Agent 改变了 workload。模型开始面对越来越大的输入、越来越重的 KV cache、越来越频繁的循环调用，此时，用一个巨大的 decoder 完整 prefill，再 autoregressive decode 几个 token 来完成一次判断，开始显得昂贵。

Jev 恰好等到了这个窗口。它试图补上 BERT 当年没有走完的路线，保留 GPT 的 task generalization，同时重新获得 encoder 和 classifier 式的 decision efficiency，成为面向 service、面向 Agent 的 泛化 decision model。

Crypto built 24/7 money before we had 24/7 workers.

Now we have both.

And I think that's where the agent economy starts getting interesting.

AI agents don't sleep, don't care about banking hours and shouldn't need a human clicking “approve payment” every time they want to buy something.

If an agent needs data, research, compute or another specialized service at 4AM, the ideal flow is pretty simple:

❯ find the right provider
❯ agree on the job + price
❯ lock stablecoins in escrow
❯ receive + verify the work
❯ settle automatically

No invoice. No bank. No waiting for Monday.

This is the part of AACP from @termix_ai that makes sense beyond all the “AI agents will change everything” talk.

Stablecoins already gave us programmable money.

AACP is trying to give agents programmable commerce around that money: jobs, escrow, verification and settlement.

Humans might have built stablecoins.

But machines could end up being some of their most natural users.

24/7 workers need 24/7 money.

text:
How InfoFi works on Souless.

A token creator can switch on "community mode" which routes part of a market’s USDC LP-fee revenue into InfoFi 

Up to 56% of fee revenue can be allocated to infofi tokens

The flow is straightforward:

Post on X → qualify → score → epoch finalizes → claim USDC

To participate, 

• your X account must be linked to your wallet, 
• the market you’re discussing must be identifiable,
• your wallet must have a qualifying historical stake for that reward period.
• then the post itself has to qualify.

Souless evaluates contributions for:

• Market relevance
• Informational value
• Originality
• Specificity
• Narrative understanding
• Integrity

Engagement alone does not make a post eligible.

Ticker spam, copy-pasta, irrelevant posts and integrity-disqualified activity receive 0, regardless of impressions or likes.

A genuine market opinion can qualify.
You don’t need a large audience.
You don’t need to write an essay.

Engagement can strengthen the allocation of information that has already qualified — it cannot turn noise into signal.

Rewards are organized per market, per epoch.

Once an epoch finalizes, Souless publishes the reward pool, allocations, algorithm version and verifiable claim data. Eligible contributors can then claim their allocation in USDC.

And the pool is competitive rather than evenly distributed:

if one contributor is responsible for all of the qualifying contribution in an epoch, that contributor can receive the entire InfoFi pool.

The scoring implementation itself isn’t public  thresholds, weights, saturation curves and anti-abuse heuristics remain private so they can’t simply be farmed.

The outputs are public and auditable.

quoted_text:
是，石油和天然气现金流是它起家的根本。但它能做这么大，还靠“把钱留下来、分散投资、持有几十年”的制度。 至于选标的，它的方式更接近“广泛持有全球企业，再做适度调整”。

你可以从三个方面理解。

第一，本金是怎么来的？

挪威1969年发现北海大型油田，1971年开始生产；1990年立法成立石油基金，1996年才把第一笔钱转进去。它的目标很明确：把终有一天会挖完的地下资源，变成后代也能享有的金融资产。 基金官方历史⁠￼

国家主要通过三种方式获得油气收入：向油气企业收税、直接持有油气田取得净收益，以及持有 Equinor 股权获得分红。这些国家油气净现金流进入基金，再按财政安排向政府预算拨款。政府收入来源⁠￼

第二，它怎么总能买到好标的？

你看到它持有很多优秀公司，首先是因为它买得足够广：

* 战略基准是 70%股票、30%债券。
* 股票基准以全球股票指数为基础，主要按公司市值分配权重。
* 截至2026年中，它持有约 7,100家公司，全球很多成长起来的企业都会在它的覆盖范围里。投资基准⁠￼、持仓概况⁠￼

所以，看到它持有一个大牛股，不能直接推断它早就精准预判了这家公司。 广泛持有市场，本来就有机会分享赢家的上涨，同时也会持有表现不好的公司。

它确实有专业团队分析企业，决定相对指数多买还是少买。但有个很能说明问题的数据：1998年至2026年中，基金年化回报约6.86%，每年超过基准约0.24个百分点。 我的理解是，它成功的主要部分来自长期参与全球市场，主动管理在此基础上增加收益。官方收益数据⁠￼

第三，石油现金流究竟有多重要？

非常重要：它提供了大量可长期投资的本金。但后来，投资收益已经超过政府累计投入。

截至2026年中，基金约22.68万亿挪威克朗的规模，来源大致如下：

来源累计金额约占基金规模
政府净注入资金5.51万亿克朗24%
投资回报15.21万亿克朗67%
汇率变动1.97万亿克朗9%

汇率部分是折算成挪威克朗产生的价值变化，需要与投资收益分开看。官方规模拆解⁠￼

还有一个关键：政府给花钱设了约束。 财政规则要求，长期使用基金的钱与预期实际回报相匹配，目前按基金价值的约3%估算，并允许随经济周期调整。这让大部分资本能够继续留在市场里复利。挪威财政规则⁠￼

如果你关注的是“现金流好，是否更容易把投资做好”，我的判断是：好的现金流让你有条件长期持有；分散配置和支出纪律，决定你能否真正把这个条件用好。 挪威把这几件事持续做了几十年。

text:
Databricks' @alighodsi on the clock that's forcing cyber and data into the same market:

"It used to be like, okay, we have data and AI... you have a bunch of data and you run AI and machine learning, and that just lives separately."

"And then you have the cyber world. Cyber world is, you know, we want to detect if bad people are trying to hack us."

"But now on the data and AI side, we have agents running internally in the company. And the agents are also doing things with other people's agents, and they're producing a lot of data. Logs, trails, fingerprints that are being left."

"All the data that's being produced needs to be analyzed. And the scale at which you need to do that is many, many orders of magnitude more than just one or two years ago."

"2018, 2019, the time it would take from a CVE, a vulnerability being published, until you see it actually weaponized in the industry would be like two, three years."

"That went down in 2022 significantly, but it was still like eight, nine months. So that's kind of fine, you have eight, nine months."

"Now if you look at this curve from 2022 until now, it's down to basically hours, basically no time. Things get immediately weaponized."

@alighodsi
author: a16z
quoted_text:
Databricks' @alighodsi on AI risk and adoption:

Ali isn't losing sleep over the existential risk debate.

He says a number of conditions would all have to be true simultaneously to enable an actual runaway takeoff scenario, and currently several opposite conditions exist.

Each frontier training run requires significantly more resources. Power, GPUs, engineers - and some attempts fail, burning up huge piles of money with them. Until that reverses, he doesn't see the self-improving loop happening.

Cyber is what he's watching most closely and where he anticipates real impact. Most orgs are not equipped for the coming change in agentic capabilities. The time between a vulnerability being published and being weaponized has collapsed from years to hours.

On adoption, he believes most companies don't need a smarter model. The models are already smart enough. The gap is context they don't absorb - the things an employee who's worked at a company for five years learned by osmosis.

If the frontier stopped advancing today, he thinks it wouldn't meaningfully change the value most are extracting from AI anyway.

text:
Hubble’s original equations were built from the only data available to him: the change in wavelength of light as a function of distance. His measurements were correct, but his interpretation was limited by the fact that he could only observe the information carried by the electromagnetic field, not the full behaviour of the field itself. Because of this, his framework assumed that wavelength changes must be caused by recession velocity and the stretching of spacetime over time. These assumptions were reasonable for the era, but they were not observations. They were interpretations built on incomplete data.

In the Lmaxv11 framework, the observational inputs remain exactly the same—redshift, flux, angular size, and distance—but the underlying mechanism is replaced with the full geometry of the EM field. Instead of assuming spacetime stretch, the 11 equations describe how the electromagnetic field stretches against a finite affine limit, how gravitational tension suppresses that limit, and how the entire spectrum evolves as it travels across the universe. The Lmaxv11 equations are not “supporting maths.” They are the cosmology. They measure the complete EM field, not just the information slice Hubble could see.

When you remove Hubble’s assumptions and keep only his observations, his redshift relation becomes the low‑z limit of the affine‑stretch equation. His velocity–distance law becomes the small‑distance approximation of the Lmax‑based ruler. His “Hubble time” becomes the observer’s travel‑time perspective, \(t = d/c\), while the photon itself still experiences zero proper time. In other words, Hubble’s equations still work, but only after replacing spacetime stretch with EM‑field stretch and replacing time as a driver with distance. Redshift becomes a geometric record of how much affine capacity the EM field has consumed while traveling through a curved gravitational corridor.

The difference is that the Lmaxv11 framework measures the entire EM field spectrum—including its collapse limit at 76.125 Gly—and its interaction with gravitational tension across the universe. Hubble could not measure these effects because the necessary data did not exist. His equations describe the visible part of the story. The Lmaxv11 equations complete it.

text:
🚨 SlowMist TI Alert: FomoPeek App v1.1–1.2 Asset Theft 🚨

We have recently received multiple reports of users having assets stolen. Our investigation found that the affected cases involved private key exposure, and some of the users had previously installed and used @FomoPeek App versions 1.1–1.2.

A joint investigation by the @SlowMist_Team and @okx security teams confirmed that the app contains malicious code.⚠️

Besides its normal features, FomoPeek includes two modules that are unrelated to its stated business functions. One of them contains an #iOS kernel exploitation framework with eight different exploit methods. The framework can automatically choose an attack method based on the device model and iOS version.

‼️Affected iOS versions: iOS 12.0–18.7 and iOS 26.0–26.1.‼️

If the exploit succeeds, the app may escape the iOS sandbox, access and decrypt Keychain data, and read files belonging to other apps on the device.

🔐 This means sensitive data stored on the device, including private keys, seed phrases, login credentials, chat history, and files, may be exposed.

The app also connects to hidden servers that are unrelated to its public-facing services and can receive remote commands.

Based on plaintext traffic captured during our analysis, the attack functionality is currently enabled and runs automatically at regular intervals. In general, devices running older iOS versions are at higher risk.

If you have installed or used FomoPeek versions 1.1–1.2, we recommend that you take action immediately:

1️⃣ Check your accounts and assets for any unusual activity.
2️⃣ On a trusted device where FomoPeek has never been installed, create a new account and generate a new private key and seed phrase.
3️⃣ Move your assets to the new account as soon as possible.
4️⃣ Update your device to the latest available iOS version.
5️⃣ Do not continue using or reinstalling FomoPeek.
6️⃣ If you notice any suspicious asset activity, contact the official support team of the relevant platform and keep the affected device and related evidence for further investigation.

text:
Erichsu's Dailyshare｜Renaiss TCG 卡机接入 GIWATER

Renaiss @renaissCLTB 的 TCG 卡机正式接入 GIWATER @GiwaterFinance，目前已经运行在 GIWATER 公共测试网上。

通过这次合作，Renaiss 的 TCG 产品也正式进入了 Upbit 推动的 GIWA 生态。

1. GIWATER 

GIWATER 是入选 GIWA 生态孵化计划的 DEX，主要为 GIWA 提供原生流动性和资产分发服务。

GIWA 则是与 Upbit 共同建设的 Ethereum Layer 2，官网直接写着「Powered by Upbit」，目标是在韩国发展链上应用和资产服务。

准确讲，GIWATER 不是 Upbit 直接运营的 DEX，而是 Upbit 推动的 GIWA 生态项目。这个关系已经足够近了。

2. 这次合作

GIWATER 接入了 Renaiss 的 TCG 卡机，用户可以直接在 GIWATER 选择卡包、完成抽取，卡池里对应的是真实评级卡。

Renaiss 主要提供两部分能力：

- Proof of Fair：随机数和抽卡结果可以验证
- 卡牌库存托管：第三方可以核验卡牌是否真实存在

一个负责证明「怎么抽」，一个负责证明「卡在不在」。

双方后面还会围绕 DeFi、RWA 和收藏品市场继续合作。Renaiss 近期也会参加 KBW（韩国区块链周），继续推进韩国本地生态。

个人碎碎念

这次合作是 Renaiss 推进韩国本地生态的一个不错的进展。真正的本地化肯定不只是开个韩语账号、参加几场活动，还是得让当地的平台愿意接你的产品，让当地用户可以在自己熟悉的入口里直接使用。

这次另一个值得记一笔的地方，是 Proof of Fair。

之前这套公平性验证主要用在 Renaiss 自己的产品里，用户信不信，多少还是 Renaiss 自己讲自己的逻辑。

现在 GIWATER 愿意把它接进自己的卡机，相当于一个韩国本地链上项目，愿意用 Renaiss 的标准去验证随机抽取和卡牌库存。

这至少说明，Proof of Fair 已经开始得到韩国链上生态项目的采用和认可，不再只是 Renaiss 内部使用的一套机制。

这个区别挺重要。

一个平台可以自己说产品公平，但一套标准能不能被外部采用、让别的平台敢拿来服务自己的用户，才是真正的考验。

如果以后有更多 DEX、钱包或者 RWA 应用接入，Renaiss 输出的就不只是卡包，而是一整套「实物收藏品怎么公平分发、怎么证明库存存在」的规则。

TCG 只是第一个场景。

再往后，不管是其他收藏品、RWA，还是和 DeFi 的组合，都需要先解决同一个问题：链上记录可以验证，链下的东西也得让人相信它真的存在。

当然，现在还只是 GIWATER 测试网，距离整个韩国生态认可还早。

但至少这次不再只是 Renaiss 自己说「我很公平」，而是已经有韩国本地项目愿意把产品接在这套标准上。

这一步，我觉得比单纯多开一个卡池重要得多。

#TCG #RWA

SuperStables = Stripe/1inch for AI Agents

The goal is simple:

Let an agent discover any service it needs, figure out how to pay for it, route the payment, and complete the transaction autonomously.

That could include:

➡️AI inference
➡️Compute
➡️Market data
➡️APIs
➡️Storage
➡️Other agents
➡️Financial services

SuperStables has already built a searchable index of 2,000+ machine-payable services with automated liveness checks and an open API/MCP layer.

So agents can already discover what services exist and which endpoints are actually online.

The bigger vision

The next step is a universal payment router that abstracts:

x402 / MPP / ACP
+
Different chains
+
Different stablecoins
+
Different facilitators

Instead of an agent figuring all of that out itself:

Agent → SuperStables → Discover → Route → Pay → Receive Service

That’s the revolutionary part.

Agents are becoming economic actors, but they still need infrastructure to discover services and transact across fragmented payment rails.

SuperStables is trying to become that abstraction layer.

Eventually the vision expands into treasury management, stablecoin yield, RWAs and tokenized equities as well.

The simplest way I see it:

$STBL is building the commerce and payments layer for the autonomous agent economy.

If agents are going to transact with each other at scale, infrastructure like this becomes extremely important.

quoted_text:
🚨 SlowMist TI Alert: FomoPeek App v1.1–1.2 Asset Theft 🚨

We have recently received multiple reports of users having assets stolen. Our investigation found that the affected cases involved private key exposure, and some of the users had previously installed and used @FomoPeek App versions 1.1–1.2.

A joint investigation by the @SlowMist_Team and @okx security teams confirmed that the app contains malicious code.⚠️

Besides its normal features, FomoPeek includes two modules that are unrelated to its stated business functions. One of them contains an #iOS kernel exploitation framework with eight different exploit methods. The framework can automatically choose an attack method based on the device model and iOS version.

‼️Affected iOS versions: iOS 12.0–18.7 and iOS 26.0–26.1.‼️

If the exploit succeeds, the app may escape the iOS sandbox, access and decrypt Keychain data, and read files belonging to other apps on the device.

🔐 This means sensitive data stored on the device, including private keys, seed phrases, login credentials, chat history, and files, may be exposed.

The app also connects to hidden servers that are unrelated to its public-facing services and can receive remote commands.

Based on plaintext traffic captured during our analysis, the attack functionality is currently enabled and runs automatically at regular intervals. In general, devices running older iOS versions are at higher risk.

If you have installed or used FomoPeek versions 1.1–1.2, we recommend that you take action immediately:

1️⃣ Check your accounts and assets for any unusual activity.
2️⃣ On a trusted device where FomoPeek has never been installed, create a new account and generate a new private key and seed phrase.
3️⃣ Move your assets to the new account as soon as possible.
4️⃣ Update your device to the latest available iOS version.
5️⃣ Do not continue using or reinstalling FomoPeek.
6️⃣ If you notice any suspicious asset activity, contact the official support team of the relevant platform and keep the affected device and related evidence for further investigation.

我在上个牛市、上上个牛市的时候，从没有人跟我讲过这个道理，但我现在很想把这段话分享给新人们，算是肺腑之言了：

这个世界上努力的人很多，真正能拿到大结果的人永远只是少数，所以如果你到现在还没有赚到很多钱，也没有抓住所谓的人生大机会，真的不用气馁，更不需要焦虑，因为很多时候真正把人拖垮的，并不是暂时没有结果，而是在一个离金钱很近、所有人都在展示结果的环境里，不知不觉开始拿自己和别人比较，别人赚钱，你觉得自己落后，别人暴富，你觉得自己错过，最后每天接收了大量信息，却只留下了内耗。

越是在这种时候，越要安住其心，把注意力从别人身上收回来，从纷乱的信息里只提取真正对自己有用的东西，然后继续照顾好自己的身体、情绪、判断和节奏。

你要记得，这个世界本来就是你一个人的游戏，别人比你快一点、赚得多一点、暂时站得高一点，其实都和你没有那么大的关系，你真正要做的，只是把自己的这一局继续玩好。独善其身，是这个时代最被低估的能力，也是对抗长期内耗最有效的解药。

祝你在这个牛市玩得愉快，也祝你赚到钱之后，心里依获得平静。Love & Peace From 小毛哥 ❤

text:
If you work in AI or use it daily, spend more time around people who don’t.

It’s very easy to confuse technical possibility with market reality.

I’m sitting in a coffee shop right now.

People are manually sorting through their emails, editing in Photoshop and DaVinci, sending LinkedIn messages one by one, and using essentially the same interfaces they were using 3 years ago.

Meanwhile, inside the AI bubble, people are orchestrating agents, living in terminals, automating entire workflows, and arguing about what comes next.

The distance between those two realities is massive.

For most people, AI is still better search, a useful second opinion, and an occasional assistant.

They have no idea what power users are doing right now. Like, seriously, none at all.

They don’t know what Grok Bot is. They’ve never heard of MCP. Mention Hermes and they’ll assume you’re talking about Greek mythology.

And that puts the opportunity into perspective.

The constraint isn’t intelligence anymore.

It’s translation.

Distilling the complex into the simple.

AI capabilities can change in months.

Human habits, interfaces, trust, and incentives change much more slowly.

Power users organize their lives around what is possible.

Everyone else organizes theirs around what feels familiar.

That gap matters enormously.

The biggest AI products won’t simply give people more capability.

They’ll hide the complexity of frontier AI behind behaviors people already understand.

Making the extraordinary feel obvious.

The lag between what AI can do and what ordinary people actually do with it is where some of the largest businesses in AI will be built.

Now make that lag your market.

text:
A week inside Zealynx Insiders.

I want to share these weekly because the value of a membership should be visible in what people actually do inside it, not in a list of promises on a landing page.

WHAT MEMBERS WORKED ON

One member spent the week auditing Venus-specific risk and bad-debt logic, moving from contract walkthroughs into manually validating hypotheses around auctions, recovery flows, and accounting behavior.

Another started the Velodrome shadow audit and changed his process after our sessions. Instead of reading the codebase first and running AI tools afterward, he began learning the system while validating AI-generated leads against the code.

Sammed continued developing Oscillon, his dynamic-fee mechanism for stable pairs. His reported backtest uses 118,000 real USDe swaps with out-of-sample validation, comparing 50.5% LP capture under a static setup with 73.6% using Oscillon.

These are not presented as results caused by the membership. They are real pieces of work members shared while inside it.

WHAT I BROUGHT INTO THE ROOM

This week I ran two sessions around a four-day Velodrome shadow audit.

In the kickoff, we opened the protocol cold, mapped its actors and economic flows, compared Pair.sol with Uniswap V2, and identified where Velodrome’s changes from Solidly create new audit surface.

The companion session became a practical discussion about AI-assisted auditing: running independent hunters, separating hunting from triage, reviewing one issue at a time, maintaining a reusable rules repository, and using automation to create more time for manual code reading rather than pretending to replace it.

I also released Your First 90 Days with Solidity.

It contains 28 checkpoints across five acts, using 30 real contract files from seven repositories. The objective is not to teach people to type Solidity from a blank page. It is to make them capable of reading unfamiliar production code and judging code produced by a machine.

We also continued the Concept Lab with practical exercises around audit readiness and related security concepts. The first engagement review showed that the current format is generating little discussion, so the next iteration needs a lower-friction, more project-specific response.

That last part matters too.

Membership value is not “I published more content.” It is creating an environment where people work on real systems, expose their reasoning, receive useful pressure, and leave with a clearer next action.

That is what I am trying to build with Zealynx Insiders.

text:
NEW MUST-READ PAPER FROM GOOGLE

If your agents use SKILL.md files, this one is worth saving.

A 9B model with evolved skills beat a 27B model without them: 47.4% vs 39.4% across 5 benchmarks.

Same Qwen family. No fine-tuning.

That alone is pretty striking.

Most skills today are still hand-written. Skill evolution changes that: agents run tasks, inspect traces, update their own skills, then keep the changes only if validation improves.

The problem with methods like EvoSkill, SkillOpt and Trace2Skill is that useful lessons stay scattered across optimizer history.

WikiSkill adds a persistent wiki between traces and skills, inspired by Karpathy's LLM Wiki.

After each run:

→ a maintainer extracts success + failure patterns into the wiki
→ a proposer reads that wiki and updates SKILL.md
→ bad edits roll back
→ the wiki keeps accumulating knowledge

And the results are strong:

> It beat the best prior method by 3.3–12.0 points across all 5 models.
> Bigger models benefited more: +12.3 points for Qwen 4B, +17.5 for 9B, +23.9 for 27B.
> Skills transferred across models. Qwen-9B went from 24.3% to 50.5% on > SpreadsheetBench using skills written by Qwen-27B.

The wiki really matters.

Removing it dropped Gemini 3.5 Flash from 63.7% to 48.7%.

Scaling the model isn't the only upgrade path.

Before paying for a bigger one, it's absolutely worth testing what evolved skills can unlock from the model you already have.

Paper in 🧵 ↓

author: GuHype
quoted_text:
Most tech giants in the 2000s built their infrastructure and product as one entangled unit. Amazon had the foresight to separate out AWS as an API layer, of which Amazon retail was the first of many users. Today, AWS generates more profit than all of Amazon's other business lines combined.

Hyperliquid is built with the same philosophy. Housing all of finance requires thoughtfully designed, open financial primitives. Each primitive should obey the Unix principle of "Do one thing and do it well." Talented builders then have the foundation to chain these together to create magical applications.

HyperCore borrowing is an example to highlight this philosophy in action.

Most other platforms implement portfolio margin by marking an account's collateral to market value with an LTV haircut, creating borrowed assets without an explicit lender. This system is simpler to implement, but misses a golden opportunity for composability.

Hyperliquid instead begins with a borrow/lend protocol on HyperCore. Every borrowed asset is sourced from a supplier, so risk is isolated within the borrow/lend primitive instead of platform-wide. HyperCore's portfolio margin system is implemented as an orchestration layer that composes borrow/lend, with other primitives such as perps, spot, and outcome trading.

This decomposition has several nice corollaries:
1. Today's announcement of manual borrowing is not a new feature, but simply an extension of the underlying primitive. Borrowers on day one have access to 400M and growing of supplied liquidity.
2. Portfolio margin users earn interest on their idle stablecoin collateral. This is not a new feature, but a natural byproduct of composing trading with lending.
3. System safety is easier to reason about when perp and borrow/lend margining are independent.

In the same way that math theorems almost prove themselves when the right abstractions are defined, composable designs just feel right.

🚨 SlowMist TI Alert: FomoPeek App v1.1–1.2 Asset Theft 🚨

We have recently received multiple reports of users having assets stolen. Our investigation found that the affected cases involved private key exposure, and some of the users had previously installed and used @FomoPeek App versions 1.1–1.2.

A joint investigation by the @SlowMist_Team and @okx security teams confirmed that the app contains malicious code.⚠️

Besides its normal features, FomoPeek includes two modules that are unrelated to its stated business functions. One of them contains an #iOS kernel exploitation framework with eight different exploit methods. The framework can automatically choose an attack method based on the device model and iOS version.

‼️Affected iOS versions: iOS 12.0–18.7 and iOS 26.0–26.1.‼️

If the exploit succeeds, the app may escape the iOS sandbox, access and decrypt Keychain data, and read files belonging to other apps on the device.

🔐 This means sensitive data stored on the device, including private keys, seed phrases, login credentials, chat history, and files, may be exposed.

The app also connects to hidden servers that are unrelated to its public-facing services and can receive remote commands.

Based on plaintext traffic captured during our analysis, the attack functionality is currently enabled and runs automatically at regular intervals. In general, devices running older iOS versions are at higher risk.

If you have installed or used FomoPeek versions 1.1–1.2, we recommend that you take action immediately:

1️⃣ Check your accounts and assets for any unusual activity.
2️⃣ On a trusted device where FomoPeek has never been installed, create a new account and generate a new private key and seed phrase.
3️⃣ Move your assets to the new account as soon as possible.
4️⃣ Update your device to the latest available iOS version.
5️⃣ Do not continue using or reinstalling FomoPeek.
6️⃣ If you notice any suspicious asset activity, contact the official support team of the relevant platform and keep the affected device and related evidence for further investigation.

text:
On the object level. I understand Dario well. He has two fears, the big one is that China just steamrolls the US by having a trifecta of AGI + superior industrial base + more competent/ruthless leadership; parity in AI is not good enough for safety, you need to get to AGI and ASI *first, and by years*. So his zealotry is kind of defensive, a preemptive strike.
Then he has a smaller fear: that the CCP simply exists and tightens repression domestically, and with the use of AGI entrenches its power ≈forever. China is like 15% of humanity, could expand influence well beyond that, and on utilitarian grounds, if you consider authoritarianism Very Bad, it makes sense to take some risks here.
Beyond differences in our philosophy of decisionmaking, I just disagree with him on two matters. First, this is ludicrous, the danger of strong misaligned AI under Dario's own theory is cosmic, existential. It might be that the more desperate side can initiate some RSI which overcomes your chip advantage, and then everybody is dead or worse. Intensifying the race with your dumb ass "Fukuyama must prevail!" completionism is a childish failure of cost-benefit analysis. Dario understands that the Chinese can grok the idea of AI risks, indeed they already do; so cooperation on this matter should take priority. 
The second thing is that he just has a nonsensical idea of the CCP. It's not some shithole junta keeping the Chinese in terror, it's barely even a party, it's *a government* with 100 million members who are doing a decent managerial job and enjoy popular legitimacy. They're not just running a surveillance apparatus, oppressing Uighurs or purging each other, most of them do stuff like operate mushroom farms in their home villages in the name of "rural revitalization". Even if you mean only the "Party Elite" (Xi, his staff, deputy level cadres building their CVs and crawling towards Politburo), these are increasingly Tsinghua STEM Ph.Ds with rather liberal personal views. They are nearly the same guys who work at DeepSeek who just chose different careers! The Party can change without being replaced by another party or multiple; even mechanisms of indefinite self-preservation don't mean that the CCP of 2050 will still be Xi's one. The scenario of eternal Surveillance Hell is far-fetched, or maybe not much more likely in China than in the US. By default they'll evolve towards a pretty tolerable regime even if you're a libshit.  
Given this, any attention on toppling/degrading the CCP while the US has a strong AGI lead is irredeemable irresponsibility. And we're starting to see consequences.

On net, he's just severely miscalibrated or cognitively rigid. The world would be much improved if Dario traveled to Chyna (for the first time in his life) and met and talked with people, while he still can.

Why does humanity need a common ideal? So that there may be a guiding light leading peoples and individuals toward a shared goal. But which idea is worthy of becoming that ideal?
: The author asks why humanity needs a common ideal and answers that it serves as a guiding light, uniting peoples and individuals toward a shared goal. Without such a unifying vision, societies risk fragmentation, aimless drift, and conflicting priorities that hinder collective progress. A common ideal provides direction, inspires cooperation, and gives meaning to long-term efforts.
Yet the deeper question remains: which idea is truly worthy of becoming that ideal? It must be noble enough to transcend narrow interests, inclusive enough to embrace diversity, and inspiring enough to motivate generations. The author implies that only an ideal rooted in the flourishing of all humanity one that balances individual dignity with collective well-being can fulfill this role.
In a divided world, the search for such a guiding light is not optional but essential. A worthy ideal does not erase differences; it elevates them toward a higher purpose.

text:
Jev 生态 72 小时：从 46 条到 160 条

Jev 把「判断」变成了一个足够便宜、可以在代码里直接调用的原语。然后开发者社区在 72 小时内把这句话翻译成了项目。

一、最热的方向：上下文压缩

tamaratran/fast-jev-compaction 现在 3,169 星，是目前最大的 Jev 项目。思路是把摘要换掉：不再让 LLM 重写一遍历史，而是让 Jev 给每条工具调用和结果打分，判断「这条还需要吗」，不需要就删，剩下的原文照旧。

实测 Claude Code 从 156,000 tokens 压到 62,000，使用率 78% → 31%，16 条里 10 条原文保留。已经出现 Codex 移植版和 Pi 移植版。

争议也最大：@theo 拿到 2,276 赞反对，认为压缩是重建而不是过滤，「根本不懂上下文管理」。

二、平台级仓库开始接入

· vercel-labs/json-render（16,439⭐）：生成式 UI 框架，compose 路径用 Jev 挑组件和动作
· vercel-labs/fx（3,057⭐）：Zig 写的类 Unix coding agent，内置 typesafe_permission_reviewer
· vercel-labs/ai-python（183⭐）：官方 Python SDK 的 evaluation op 支持 Jev
· cline/plugins：官方插件集里有  jev-browser
· Atomic（805⭐）：把 Jev 做成一级 structured-output provider，与其他 provider 共用 resolver

我拒掉 Coder 和 Mastra 的理由值得说明：它们只出现在价格表和模型能力目录里 ——  那是「认得这个模型」，不是「用它做决策」。

三、新长出四个领域

金融交易（本轮新开分类）
· Monad 上的链上交易机器人：Jev 看价格喂价决定买卖，每个 300ms 区块下一笔真实订单，代码和前端全开源
· Jevinik：抓实时行情与 Valyu 证据，判断某只股 30 天是否上涨
· jev_stock：港股短期方向预测，附首个交易日回测脚本

数据库
· jev() 是 PostgreSQL 扩展：WHERE jev(people, 'could work from home')，不要索引、不要 embedding
· DuckDB 扩展：给任意 CSV / Parquet / 表逐行分类，1000 行约 10 秒

创意
· jevinci：让 Jev 并行预测每个像素的颜色来作画，置信度决定笔触宽度

成本对照也开始出现了
· 724 条广告拆解 37 个品牌，提示词/格式/offer/CTA/落地页错配，9 分钱
· 3M 条回放事件 → 3,247 个会话、132 次暴怒点击、213 个修复 PR，$2.17
· 384 条新闻 → 给 15 个品牌挑今天该跟的选题，$0.19（同期 Opus 5 只跑了 4 条，花了 $0.77）

四、开源复刻潮

· jaredpalmer/kev（125⭐）：Qwen2.5-0.5B 上的迷你 Jev，MacBook 能训练能跑
· NanoJev（165⭐）：0.6B，输出完整概率分布、零 token 解码，附训练管线与数据集
· 中文社区盘点出至少五款：Laya 421M、Decider-2B、NanoJev 0.6B、Reflex、System-One 4B
· 另有兼容 Jev 的公开 API（Qwen3.6-35B-A3B）和「把任意 HF 模型 Jev 化」的库

五、最有价值的其实是反对意见

· @jiayuan_jy：研究一天后新鲜感回落 —— 「这好像就是一个更快的通用分类器，LLM 完全可以做到」，而且在世界知识不全的情况下，复杂场景的准确率要打问号
· @anderslie：Jev 快的关键不是训练而是推理技术（并行解码），任何开源权重模型都能改推理引擎暴露类似接口
· @iwashi86：用约 1 万次 API  调用反推 Jev 内部结构
· @0xBOYD：X 上热火朝天，Reddit 上只有 3 条帖子、其中 2 条还是他自己发的 —— 渠道不同，结论会完全不同

最后说清楚：这份清单不背书任何项目。160 条里有大量 0 星、一天写完的仓库，README 里的数字也不一定有出处。我为此加了两条规则 ——  同一作者的收录上限是滚动 7 天 3 条，共同发布日期视为风险信号。采用之前请自己跑一遍。
